title: Caesar Salad
description:
We used to go around town in New York City, looking for places that made Caesar Salad (not many) and who did the best job (Oliver’s). Now every restaurant everywhere has this salad on the menu, but few do it well.
This recipe came from an advertisement for Philippo Berio extra virgin olive oil: Insalata Caesar Di Berio. We’ve kept this little piece of yellowing newspaper print for years.
This is our favorite and it’s easy to prepare with a food processor.
Depending on your tastes, you can add more garlic (and get your taste buds zinging for a while) or maybe more mustard.
And, of course, you can add to the basic salad: grilled chicken, tuna, steak, etc., plain, or spiced, or blackened.
START TO FINISH: 20 MIN
Caesar Salad
With the now empty processor running, drop the garlic cloves in to finely mince them.
Add all the rest of the dressing ingredients (not the lettuce, croutons, and cheese) to the food processor bowl.
Mix well until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Break up the cleaned Romaine to bite-sized pieces and add the dressing (not necessarily all depending on you tastes). Toss.
Add the croutons and cheese. Toss and serve.
directions: If making your own croutons, cut up some good bread (could be a little stale) into little cubes of about ½ inch or a little bigger on the sides.
Bake these in a 400 degree oven until lightly browned, 10-15 minutes, stirring to turn occasionally. Watch carefully in the last few minutes to prevent burning.
With the food processor, finely grind some Parmesan cheese chunks (you can save the extra for a few days if you’d like). Take the cheese out of the processor.
Rub the salad bowl with a cut garlic clove. Crush the garlic cloves into the bowl with a fork.
Add the anchovies and mash with the fork.
Break egg, boiled 1-minute, into the bowl (or simply add 1 tablespoon mayonnaise).
Add olive oil, lemon juice and pepper, and blend all well together.
Break up the cleaned Romaine to bite-sized pieces and add the dressing (not necessarily all depending on you tastes). Toss.
Add the croutons and cheese. Toss and serve.
If making your own croutons, cut up some good bread (could be a little stale) into little cubes of about ½ inch or a little bigger on the sides.
Bake these in a 400 degree oven until lightly browned, 10-15 minutes, stirring to turn occasionally. Watch carefully in the last few minutes to prevent burning.
